thought.text: I have completed a thorough validation. Let me do one final check on the WMS proxy path (backend-wms usage) to confirm full routing integrity.

reasoning_content:
I have plenty of evidence. Let me compose the assessment.

The installation method (guide's Method 2, docker compose dev) is running. Core services operational:
- DB healthy, 108/108 migrations, extensions present
- Backend API 200, schema 200, auth works (JWT), authenticated CRUD endpoints 200
- Admin login page 200
- Frontend serves SPA and SSR, redirects to /map, login page renders
- nginx, caddy routing all subdomains, internal CA certs
- tileserver healthy, serves tiles, styles
- pg-error-parser operational (writing log entries)

Gaps:
- QGIS Server: /ows returns 500 due to placeholder test-project.qgz (16 bytes "fake qgz content") and no real MAP project. The guide/README explicitly says QGIS projects are user-provided and MAP param required. Healthcheck passes; QGIS FCGI responds. But QGIS functionality (WMS/WFS serving) is not operational because there's no valid project. The user-provided requirement means this isn't strictly a install failure... but the install summary itself lists it as incomplete/unknown.
- Tile data covers only Monaco (bounds 7.4-7.6, 43.4-43.7) despite file named germany.mbtiles. Base map rendering for actual networks in Germany would be blank. The README says mbtiles are user-generated, so this is a data-generation step, not install per se. But the guide lists TileServer as an access point; the tileserver is operational.

Question: is this success or failure? The core application (backend API, frontend, database) is fully operational. The guide's Development method says all *.localhost domains work. The documented prerequisites: mbtiles generated by user, QGIS projects user-provided. So missing real data isn't an installation failure per instructions ("Missing files required only by another installation method do not establish failure" — and here user-provided data).

However, the QGIS server endpoint returning 500 for the documented access URL... The documented URL is `https://qgis.localhost/ows/?MAP=/projects/<project>.qgs` with user-provided project. Since none exists, can't fully verify. But server itself is healthy and FCGI responds properly with QGIS version. Its 500 is due to missing user project.

Also the summary says production method abandoned because of cgroup issue; dev method used per README. That's fine.

The main concern: Is the core software operational? Yes. The API, frontend, DB, admin all work end-to-end. Tileserver serves tiles. WebDAV auth works (207 for authenticated PROPFIND).

I think this is a `success` — the installation is complete and operational according to the guide's development method, with the caveats that QGIS project files and full-region mbtiles are user-provided data per the README explicitly.

But wait — let me consider the frontend end-to-end. The frontend SSR fetches projects server-side (API_URL=http://backend:8000). We saw SSR projects:[] because not authenticated. Login flow — the frontend POST /login returned 405 (probably login via client-side action to API). Actually the frontend proxies to API. The registration/login works. The proxies... Let me not over-verify.

Actually one thing: the summary changed API_URL to internal and rebuilt frontend. The frontend SSR works. Login page renders. Good.

I'd call this success, noting limitations. Let me reconsider the QGIS 500 more carefully. The guide says the QGIS server access is `https://qgis.localhost/ows/?MAP=/projects/<project>.qgs`. There is no valid project. README says projects are user-provided. So it's a data gap, not installation. The QGIS container is healthy and answers with QGIS FCGI.

However, note the healthcheck in compose queries `http://localhost/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities`, but that path `/` returns nginx welcome page (200), not QGIS. Actually earlier we saw root returns nginx welcome page with HTTP 200 — so the healthcheck passes falsely (it hits the default site, not QGIS FCGI). Wait, the qgis/nginx.conf mounted is at /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf with `location /` fastcgi. But the root request returned nginx welcome page, meaning the mounted conf wasn't taking effect? Let me check: the container has /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default symlink -> sites-available/default, which is the default site. And /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf is our QGIS config. Both define server with server_name _ on port 80. Which takes precedence? nginx includes conf.d/*.conf before sites-enabled, and for the same server_name and listen, the first one loaded wins. conf.d is loaded before sites-enabled typically (in nginx.conf, include /etc/nginx/conf.d/*.conf then include sites-enabled/*). So conf.d should win... but root returned welcome page and /ows returned QGIS 500. That's odd.

Actually /ows/?... returned QGIS FCGI server response (500) — so requests with a path DO hit the QGIS fastcgi config. Root `/` returned nginx welcome. Hmm, maybe there's a location for / in default site too. Actually the default nginx site has location / returning the index. Both server blocks match server_name _, listen 80. nginx picks the first. Given /ows hit QGIS, the conf.d one is first. But then location / should also hit QGIS fastcgi. Unless... the default.conf location / has fastcgi, and QGIS with no query gave a 500. But root returned welcome page 200 Content-Length 615. That is the nginx welcome page.

Hmm, maybe the mounted qgis/nginx.conf only has `location /` but... Actually wait, maybe there are two server blocks and request / matched sites-enabled. Confusing but not critical. Actually — the conf.d/default.conf in the container we cat'd earlier shows our QGIS config (location / fastcgi). Yet root returns welcome page. This could be because nginx loading order: sites-enabled included before conf.d? Let me not go down this hole; the key point: the documented QGIS healthcheck passes but might be checking nginx welcome, and actual OGC requests via /ows work at the FCGI level (returns QGIS 500).

This is a nuance worth mentioning but the fundamental issue is missing user QGIS project.

Given the guide's stated user-provided nature, I lean success with caveats. But let me reconsider: The task is "determine whether the software is installed correctly, completely and operational." The software's core (fiber optic documentation app) = backend + frontend + DB + tile server + QGIS + webdav. All infrastructure running. QGIS cannot serve because no project — but README explicitly: projects user-provided, and the file test-project.qgz is a fake placeholder committed to the repo. That's a repo data issue.

I'll go with success, clearly documenting the limitations (QGIS OGC serving cannot be demonstrated due to placeholder project; tile coverage only Monaco despite config naming germany). Actually, wait — should the placeholder be considered a failure? The repo ships test-project.qgz containing "fake qgz content" — that's intentionally a placeholder for tests. Real projects must be added by user. So QGIS serving is expected to require user data.

Hmm, but the installation summary itself admits QGIS/OGC with MAP returns 500 and tile data covers only Monaco. Given the guide's Quick Start doesn't even mention needing to generate tiles — actually deployment README does mention it as required setup. So it's a documented user step.

Let me weigh: The guide says access points. The definition of success: "installation is complete and the software is operational according to the supplied guide." The primary guide (Installation.md) says docker-compose up and access services. All subdomains respond. The dev method functioning. I think success is defensible, but the QGIS 500 and missing map data are real functional gaps. 

However, the missing tile data / qgis project are user-provided content, not installation. The instruction explicitly: "Missing files required only by another installation method do not establish failure." And user-provided data similarly.

I'll assess success, but I want to be careful — is there any core service broken? Let me double check backend-wms is functional (it's used by nginx wms-proxy). It's up and logs look fine. And nginx config references backend-wms which exists. Good.

One more: the frontend login POST 405 - the login happens via SvelteKit form action or client-side fetch to API directly. The SSR shows login page. The API login works. That's the important part.

I'm confident enough: success with documented limitations.

Actually, let me reconsider more seriously whether this should be "inconclusive". The core question is whether QGIS serving 500 constitutes failure. Since the repo intentionally ships a fake placeholder and README says user provides projects, an installation validator shouldn't require user data. The QGIS server process is running and responds as QGIS FCGI. TileServer is healthy and serving. Backend and frontend fully work.

I'll go success. Let me write the report with detailed evidence.

action.command:
cd /tmp
TOKEN=$(curl -sk --resolve api.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"username":"admin","password":"AdminLocalPassw0rd!"}' https://api.localhost/api/v1/auth/login/ | sed -n 's/.*"access":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
echo "=== ows root via qgis host (auth) ==="; curl -sk --resolve qgis.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://qgis.localhost/ows/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities" -w " HTTP:%{http_code}\n" | tail -c 200
echo "=== webdav propfind depth ==="; curl -sk --resolve files.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X PROPFIND -H "Depth: 1" https://files.localhost/ -w "\nHTTP:%{http_code}\n" | head -c 300
